transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As we discussed, Press 3 is available for a controlled pilot using the two identified billet lots of recycled aluminum alloy. The goal is to produce enclosure housings for engineering evaluation only — this is not a routine production approval. Before I release the pilot configuration, I want to make sure we go through the standard pre-pilot review and get input from each of your areas: quality, process engineering, maintenance, and EHS. Let's walk through what each of you needs to see or flag so we can proceed with the right controls in place.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something for the pilot configuration. In the customer's pilot control plan — which I received in yesterday's customer portal update but hasn't yet been uploaded to the internal work order — all pilot housings require a 100% conductivity test, and 24 housings must be retained for evaluation. We need to make sure those requirements are captured in the work order before the configuration is released.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share results from my process trial on this recycled alloy. Each furnace charge can produce at most 240 acceptable housings, so to meet the pilot's needs we should authorize exactly 480 total housings from two charges. Also, each charge requires a 2-hour preheat. I should note my test note is still awaiting materials-review signoff, but I wanted to get this in front of everyone now so the pilot configuration reflects the correct charge limits and preheat requirements.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag something from my inspection of Press 3. I found a cracked insert in the enclosure die that must be replaced before the pilot. The replacement and verification will require exactly 5 hours of downtime. I haven't entered this finding in the maintenance scheduling system yet, but everyone should know about it now so we can plan the downtime into the pilot schedule.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag an EHS permit condition for this pilot. My permit review — clarified by the environmental permitting office this morning — found that recycled-alloy fines must be collected in exactly 2 sealed scrap bins and transferred under a waste manifest. I have not yet amended the area permit board to reflect this, but this requirement needs to be captured as a control in the pilot configuration before it's released.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Customer pilot control plan requirements — 100% conductivity test and 24 retained housings — must be captured in the internal work order before configuration release.

Process trial test note must receive materials-review signoff and charge limits (240 acceptable housings per charge, 480 total) and 2-hour preheat per charge must be reflected in the pilot configuration.
Cracked die insert must be replaced and verified, requiring 5 hours of downtime, and this finding must be entered in the maintenance scheduling system before the pilot proceeds.
Area permit board must be amended to reflect the requirement for 2 sealed scrap bins and waste manifest transfer for recycled-alloy fines before the pilot configuration is released.
